--- header_pre ---
#define j0 _j0

#define yn _yn

#define lgamma _lgamma
#define tgamma _tgamma

#ifndef M_PI

#endif

static float g_angle = 0.0f;
static int   g_rotating = 0;

--- display_header ---
void display(void) {
  glClear(GL_COLOR_BUFFER_BIT | GL_DEPTH_BUFFER_BIT);
  glLoadIdentity();
  glPushAttrib(GL_ALL_ATTRIB_BITS);
  float A[8], B[8], C[8];
--- render_state ---
  glEnable(GL_MULTISAMPLE);
  glDisable(GL_LINE_SMOOTH);
--- camera ---
  glTranslatef(0.0000f, 0.0000f, -19.0000f);
  glRotatef(30.0000f, 1.0f, 0.0f, 0.0f);
  glRotatef(0.0000f, 0.0f, 1.0f, 0.0f);
  glTranslatef(-0.0000f, -0.0000f, -0.0000f);
--- header_post ---
--- source ---
  static float th, px, py, pz, orbitR; // shared orbit scratch
  static float EARTH_R = 0.17;
  static float EARTH_RATE = 0.85;
  static float ORB_BASE = 0;
  static float ORB_SCALE = 10;

  OrbitRings(Drel, tilt) {
    orbitR = ORB_BASE + ORB_SCALE*log(1 + Drel);
    glBegin(GL_LINE_LOOP);
      for(i, 0, 96) {
        glVertex3f(cos(i*TAU/96)*orbitR, sin(i*TAU/96)*orbitR*sin(tilt), sin(i*TAU/96)*orbitR*cos(tilt));
      }
    glEnd();
  }
  // planet(): one lit sphere on an inclined circular orbit. The caller passes
  // TRUE ratios relative to Earth: distance from Sun (Drel), year length (Yrel),
  // and body radius (Rrel). The display applies documented compression for
  // orbit distance, orbit speed, and sphere size so the system fits on screen.
  // th/px/py/pz stay set after the call so the caller can hang a label off the
  // body.
  planet(Drel, Yrel, phase, incl, Rrel, cr, cg, cb) {
    orbitR = ORB_BASE + ORB_SCALE*log(1 + Drel);
    th = t*(EARTH_RATE/pow(Yrel, 1.0/3.0)) + phase;
    px = cos(th)*orbitR;
    py = sin(th)*orbitR*sin(incl);
    pz = sin(th)*orbitR*cos(incl);
    glEnable(GL_LIGHTING);
    glColor3f(cr, cg, cb);
    glPushMatrix();
      glTranslatef(px, py, pz);
      glutSolidSphere(EARTH_R * pow(Rrel, 1.0/3.0), 24, 18);
    glPopMatrix();
    glDisable(GL_LIGHTING);
  }
  glMaterialfv(GL_FRONT_AND_BACK, GL_SPECULAR, (GLfloat[]){0.35, 0.33, 0.3, 1});
  glMaterialfv(GL_FRONT_AND_BACK, GL_SHININESS, (GLfloat[]){18});
  glClearColor(0.02, 0.02, 0.05, 1);
  glEnable(GL_NORMALIZE);
  glEnable(GL_CULL_FACE);
  glEnable(GL_DEPTH_TEST);

  // planets: opaque, lit by the central SOLAR light. Blending stays OFF here
  // so each body is a solid sphere - planets never blend with one another.
  // Only the sun's corona (drawn last, additive) glows over them. glColor
  // rides GL_COLOR_MATERIAL and one shared specular material gives every body
  // a sun-glint.
  glEnable(GL_LIGHT0);
  glEnable(GL_COLOR_MATERIAL);
  // Body sizes: R/E is the true radius relative to Earth; "display" is what
  // this scene draws after the cube-root squash (display = EARTH_R*R/E^(1/3)),
  // which keeps the 0.38..11x planet span legible. The Sun (109x!) is off the
  // chart, so it stays a hand-tuned "hero" size rather than on the planet rule.
  //   +---------+--------+---------+
  //   | Body    |   R/E  | display |
  //   +---------+--------+---------+
  //   | Mercury |  0.383 |  0.124  |
  //   | Venus   |  0.950 |  0.167  |
  //   | Earth   |  1.000 |  0.170  |
  //   | Mars    |  0.532 |  0.138  |
  //   | Jupiter | 10.97  |  0.378  |
  //   | Saturn  |  9.14  |  0.356  |
  //   | Uranus  |  3.98  |  0.269  |
  //   | Neptune |  3.86  |  0.267  |
  //   | Sun     | 109.2  |  hero   |
  //   +---------+--------+---------+
  //
  // Orbit speeds: Y/E is the true year length relative to Earth, but planet()
  // displays angular rate with a cube-root squash:
  // rate = EARTH_RATE/Y/E^(1/3). That keeps the compressed orbits readable
  // instead of making the outer planets look detached.
  // | Body    | Year length relative to Earth |
  // | ------- | ----------------------------: |
  // | Mercury |                     **0.241** |
  // | Venus   |                     **0.615** |
  // | Earth   |                     **1.000** |
  // | Mars    |                     **1.881** |
  // | Jupiter |                     **11.86** |
  // | Saturn  |                     **29.46** |
  // | Uranus  |                      **84.0** |
  // | Neptune |                     **164.8** |
  // | Sun     |                       **N/A** |
  //
  // Orbit distances: D/E is the true mean distance from the Sun relative to
  // Earth. planet() and OrbitRings() display it with a log scale:
  // orbitR = ORB_BASE + ORB_SCALE*log(1 + D/E). The larger base offset pushes
  // the inner system outward, while the log term spreads Mercury/Venus/Earth
  // more than a cube-root fit and keeps Neptune near the frame edge. The Sun
  // stays at the origin and does not use the orbit formula.
  // | Body    | Distance from Sun relative to Earth |
  // | ------- | ----------------------------------: |
  // | Mercury |                           **0.387** |
  // | Venus   |                           **0.723** |
  // | Earth   |                           **1.000** |
  // | Mars    |                           **1.524** |
  // | Jupiter |                           **5.203** |
  // | Saturn  |                           **9.537** |
  // | Uranus  |                           **19.19** |
  // | Neptune |                           **30.07** |
  // | Sun     |                     **0.000 / N/A** |
  // Mercury (0.383 Earth radii, 0.241 Earth years)
  planet(0.387, 0.241, 0.0, 0.18, 0.383, 0.63, 0.58, 0.54);
  glColor3f(0.9, 0.85, 0.8);
  glRasterPos3f(px + 0.14, py + 0.16, pz);
  label("Mercury");
  // Venus (0.950 Earth radii, 0.615 Earth years)
  planet(0.723, 0.615, 1.0, 0.06, 0.950, 0.93, 0.81, 0.55);
  glColor3f(1, 0.9, 0.65);
  glRasterPos3f(px + 0.2, py + 0.22, pz);
  label("Venus");
  // Earth (the reference radius) + Moon circling it
  planet(1.000, 1.000, 2.5, 0.0, 1.000, 0.3, 0.52, 0.95);
  glPushMatrix();
    glTranslatef(px, py, pz);
    glRotatef(t*160, 0, 1, 0);
    glTranslatef(0.25, 0.06, 0);
    glEnable(GL_LIGHTING);
    glColor3f(0.72, 0.72, 0.7);
    glutSolidSphere(0.046, 12, 10);
    glDisable(GL_LIGHTING);
  glPopMatrix();
  glColor3f(0.6, 0.8, 1);
  glRasterPos3f(px + 0.2, py + 0.22, pz);
  label("Earth");
  // Mars (0.532 Earth radii, 1.881 Earth years)
  planet(1.524, 1.881, 4.0, 0.22, 0.532, 0.88, 0.45, 0.26);
  glColor3f(1, 0.6, 0.45);
  glRasterPos3f(px + 0.16, py + 0.18, pz);
  label("Mars");
  // Jupiter (10.97 Earth radii, 11.86 Earth years)
  planet(5.203, 11.86, 1.8, 0.05, 10.97, 0.83, 0.69, 0.52);
  glColor3f(1, 0.85, 0.65);
  glRasterPos3f(px + 0.62, py + 0.5, pz);
  label("Jupiter");
  // Saturn (9.14 Earth radii, 29.46 Earth years) + two ring bands with a
  // Cassini gap.
  // Rings are translucent flat strips, so blending is on (additive, like the
  // corona) and culling is off while they draw - either face may point at the
  // camera. Depth writes are masked so the bands don't clip each other.
  planet(9.537, 29.46, 3.4, 0.10, 9.14, 0.9, 0.8, 0.58);
  glPushMatrix();
    glTranslatef(px, py, pz);
    glRotatef(27, 1, 0, 0.35);
    glDisable(GL_CULL_FACE);
    glEnable(GL_BLEND);
    glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE);
    glDepthMask(GL_FALSE);
    glBegin(GL_TRIANGLE_STRIP);
      for(s, 0, 33) {
        glColor4f(0.85, 0.75, 0.55, 0.5);
        glVertex3f(cos(s*TAU/32)*0.66, 0, sin(s*TAU/32)*0.66);
        glColor4f(0.9, 0.82, 0.6, 0.3);
        glVertex3f(cos(s*TAU/32)*0.88, 0, sin(s*TAU/32)*0.88);
      }
    glEnd();
    glBegin(GL_TRIANGLE_STRIP);
      for(s, 0, 33) {
        glColor4f(0.8, 0.72, 0.5, 0.35);
        glVertex3f(cos(s*TAU/32)*0.93, 0, sin(s*TAU/32)*0.93);
        glColor4f(0.75, 0.68, 0.48, 0.12);
        glVertex3f(cos(s*TAU/32)*1.05, 0, sin(s*TAU/32)*1.05);
      }
    glEnd();
    glDepthMask(GL_TRUE);
    glDisable(GL_BLEND);
    glEnable(GL_CULL_FACE);
  glPopMatrix();
  glColor3f(1, 0.9, 0.7);
  glRasterPos3f(px + 1.1, py + 0.4, pz);
  label("Saturn");
  // Uranus (3.98 Earth radii, 84.0 Earth years) + a thin ring standing nearly on
  // end:
  // the planet is tipped ~98 degrees, so its rings face the sun pole-on
  planet(19.19, 84.0, 5.2, 0.07, 3.98, 0.58, 0.82, 0.88);
  glPushMatrix();
    glTranslatef(px, py, pz);
    glRotatef(98, 0, 0, 1);
    glDisable(GL_CULL_FACE);
    glEnable(GL_BLEND);
    glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE);
    glDepthMask(GL_FALSE);
    glBegin(GL_TRIANGLE_STRIP);
      for(s, 0, 33) {
        glColor4f(0.72, 0.88, 0.92, 0.4);
        glVertex3f(cos(s*TAU/32)*0.44, 0, sin(s*TAU/32)*0.44);
        glColor4f(0.72, 0.88, 0.92, 0.1);
        glVertex3f(cos(s*TAU/32)*0.58, 0, sin(s*TAU/32)*0.58);
      }
    glEnd();
    glDepthMask(GL_TRUE);
    glDisable(GL_BLEND);
    glEnable(GL_CULL_FACE);
  glPopMatrix();
  glColor3f(0.75, 0.92, 0.95);
  glRasterPos3f(px + 0.6, py + 0.35, pz);
  label("Uranus");
  // Neptune (3.86 Earth radii, 164.8 Earth years)
  planet(30.07, 164.8, 0.7, 0.14, 3.86, 0.28, 0.42, 0.9);
  glColor3f(0.55, 0.65, 1);
  glRasterPos3f(px + 0.42, py + 0.34, pz);
  label("Neptune");
  // live readout: Earth's orbital phase, anchored in 3D below the system
  glColor3f(0.75, 0.8, 0.9);
  glRasterPos3f(-2.6, -5.6, 0);
  label("Earth phase = %f", fmod(t*EARTH_RATE + 2.5, TAU));

  // faint orbit rings (unlit lines), one per planet at its inclination
  glDisable(GL_LIGHTING);
  glColor3f(0.22, 0.24, 0.34);
  glLineWidth(1.2);
  OrbitRings(0.387, 0.18);
  OrbitRings(0.723, 0.06);
  OrbitRings(1.000, 0.0);
  OrbitRings(1.524, 0.22);
  OrbitRings(5.203, 0.05);
  OrbitRings(9.537, 0.10);
  OrbitRings(19.19, 0.07);
  OrbitRings(30.07, 0.14);

  // the sun, drawn LAST so its soft corona composites over the rest of the
  // scene: an additive glow (GL_ONE) that is still depth-tested - planets in
  // front of the sun occlude it, planets behind it receive the glow (so only
  // the corona blends with the planets). Depth writes are masked so the
  // stacked shells don't clip each other; the opaque core then writes depth.
  // Drawn unlit so it glows (it sits on the SOLAR light at the origin).
  glEnable(GL_BLEND);
  glBlendFunc(GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE);
  glDepthMask(GL_FALSE);
  // soft corona, then two pulsing shells at different frequencies
  glColor4f(1, 0.72, 0.22, 0.16);
  glutSolidSphere(0.72 + sin(t*1.3)*0.02, 24, 24);
  glColor4f(1, 0.85, 0.3, 0.5);
  glutSolidSphere(0.56 + cos(2*t)*0.012, 24, 24);
  glutSolidSphere(0.5 + sin(t)*0.012, 24, 24);
  glDepthMask(GL_TRUE);
  glutSolidSphere(0.45, 24, 24);
  glDisable(GL_BLEND);
  glColor3f(1, 0.9, 0.5);
  glRasterPos3f(0.62, 0.58, 0);
  label("Sun");
